description: The museum centrepiece. Victory Aircraft Lancaster Mk X FM159 stood on concrete pedestals beside Highway 2 at Nanton for decades before being brought indoors and restored; all four Merlins are run several times a year. Displayed as F2-T and dedicated to Calgary-born Ian W. Bazalgette VC of 635 Squadron.
aliases: Lancaster X; Lancaster Mk X; Avro 683; F2-T

description: RCAF Anson Mk II; silverhawkauthor cites both 886 and 7481 for this airframe, the former probably a construction number.

description: Airspeed Oxford held by the museum together with four further derelict centre sections in storage; no complete restored airframe reported.

description: CF-100 Mk 3D built at Malton in 1954; served with 3 OTU as JF-152 and with 428 and 432 Squadrons and the Electronic Warfare Unit, then stood at CFB Suffield 1968-1994. Mounted on a pylon at the museum.

description: Cessna Crane c/n 3760 built in 1942 and used by the US military in the Second World War. One of three Cranes acquired by Lloyd Drake of Lundbreck; restored to flyable condition in 2002 by his son Loren, who donated it in 2018. To be painted BCATP yellow and kept taxiable.
aliases: T50; T-50; Crane; UC-78; Bobcat; UC78

description: RCAF Tiger Moth 1204, c/n 1405, registered C-FCIX and airworthy.

Mosquito PR Mk 35 RS700, once Spartan Air Services CF-HMS. Owned by the City of Calgary, championed by the Calgary Mosquito Society and moved to the museum's North Hangar on 11 August 2012, where it is under restoration with the Merlins being brought to running condition.
Fairchild PT-26 Cornell 14424, displayed complete but unrestored.
aliases: Cornell; PT-26; PT26; M-62; Cornell II; M62

description: Fleet Fawn Mk II c/n 123, ex-RCAF 264, donated by Ernie and Agnes Oakman; taxiable with a runnable engine.

Halifax reconstruction project assembled from parts sourced from dive sites, the RAF Museum and elsewhere, including a propeller blade, bomb-bay doors and an instrument panel. No complete airframe; the museum also supports the search for LW170 off the Shetland Islands.

Spanish-built Bf 109 derivative c/n 164, Spanish Air Force 12E-265 / C.4K-114, used in the 1969 film Battle of Britain. Bought from Spitfire Productions in 1967 for the Canadian War Museum, restored 1984-86 in Spanish Air Force markings, later loaned to the Western Canada Aviation Museum and now on loan from the Canada Aviation and Space Museum to Nanton. Tail left blank because the Canada Aviation and Space Museum records the same Spanish serial on a Buchon of a different construction number; the two attributions conflict and one is wrong.

Full-size Bf 109 mock-up with a working canopy and fully equipped cockpit using some original instruments, built by Lech Lebiedowski from parts salvaged at a crash site. Painted as a Jagdgeschwader 27 machine in 1942-43 Mediterranean colours. A mock-up, not an original airframe.
Restored and operational Link trainer complete with instructor's table. A ground trainer rather than an airframe.
aliases: Link Trainer; ANT-18; Blue Box; ANT18

description: RCAF Yale 3404, ex-USAAC 64-2157, donated to the Nanton Lancaster Society in 1995 by Jon Spinks. A new engine has been fitted and the rear fuselage re-skinned and the forward fuselage framework restored, but the museum states the aircraft is currently in storage. The only Yale here; silverhawkauthor also lists 3390 at Nanton, which the museum's own pages contradict.

Reproduction Spitfire Mk IX being built around original Spitfire parts gathered from Malta, Australia, New Zealand, Burma, the Netherlands, France and England, with a Merlin 68. To be finished in D-Day invasion markings honouring Nanton-born twins Bruce and Douglas Warren.
aliases: Spitfire; Spitfire IX; Spitfire Mk IX

description: Five-eighths-scale Spitfire replica marked SK-F / SK-M.
